trace.history_context:
Student: Does an incomplete grade remain an I forever?
Assistant (context only): An incomplete ("I") grade does not remain an "I" forever; if it is not changed to an earned grade, it will automatically convert to an "F" grade after a fixed time set by the competent authority .

Student: My CGPA is exactly 2.00. Am I below the academic-warning threshold?
Assistant (context only): A CGPA of exactly 2.00 is not below the academic-warning threshold . The minimum CGPA required to avoid an academic warning for undergraduate programs is 2.00, and an academic warning is only issued if the CGPA drops below 2.00 at the end of a semester .

Student: What happens if my CGPA remains below 2.00 for three consecutive semesters?
Assistant (context only): If your CGPA remains below 2.00 for three consecutive semesters, your warning count becomes three and your admission at the University is automatically closed  . Admission closure results in the termination of your studies at the University .

Student: After two warnings, my CGPA becomes 2.10. What happens to my warning count?
Assistant (context only): If your CGPA equals or exceeds 2.00 after the 1st or 2nd academic warning, your warning count is reset to zero . Therefore, if your CGPA rises to 2.10 after having two warnings, your warning count will be reset to zero .

Student: I am on my second academic warning. Can I register for a new course?
Assistant (context only): Students on their second academic warning must not register for a new course unless it is recommended by the Head of Department (HoD) and approved by the Controller of Examinations .

**Related conditions and exceptions from the retrieved sources:**

> A student under academic warning or probation: a) Must register for all such courses, in whi ch the grade was F, provided these courses are being offered. b) Should register for all such courses, in which the grade was D, D + or C-, provided these courses are b eing offered. c) Should not register for more than five courses. 

Student: I failed theory but passed its associated lab. What must I repeat?
Assistant (context only): If a student fails in theory but passes the lab, both the theory and the lab parts must be repeated .

rechecking.question: How soon must I apply for final-exam rechecking, is there a fee, and when is it refunded?
rechecking.answer:
Applications for final-exam rechecking must reach the Examination Office within seven days of the announcement of the result [S1]. 

A prescribed fee is required to be submitted with the rechecking application on the prescribed form [S2] [S4], which also applies to students who have not viewed their final exam paper in the scheduled paper viewing session [S1]. The rechecking fee will be refunded if there is an increase in marks [S1].

VI – SEMESTER RULES 
1. Dates/week of sessional exams and the final exam are 
announced at the commencement of the semester. 
Students are not allowed to miss any of the sessional 
and/or the final exams. No credit for the missed exams 
would be given to the student. 
2. Students are allowed to apply online for the retake of any 
missed exam due to hospitalization, accident, or family 
emergencies such as the death or marriage of a blood 
relative. They must provide valid proof for any of these 
reasons. Please note that a mere medical certificate will 
not be accepted for this facility. 
3. Students are strongly advised to avoid scheduling any 
personal events during the examination period. However, 
in case of a clash with an event, the co mmittee may 
review the request based on submitted evidence and 
decide accordingly. 
4. Please note that clashes due to Umrah or Itikaf will not be 
considered, as these are not mandatory requirements. 
5. In all cases, the Director is the final authority who would,  
after consultation with the concerned faculty member (s), 
give a decision within one week from the date of 
submission of the application. 
6. Students are allowed to Add/Drop a course during the 
first two weeks of the commencement of the semester. 
However, students admitted in First semester shall not be 
allowed to Add/Drop a course. Students are advised to 
attend all the classes of courses they intend to take 
during the semester. No add/drop requests will be 
entertained after the last date.

II - FINANCIAL RULES 
Fee Structure and Mode of Payment 
The fee is charged on Semester basis, and it becomes due two 
weeks earlier than the start of a semester at the time of course 
registration.  
Fees are paid in the bank through bank challan available in 
Accounts Office/Flex. 
All fees are non-Refundable 
All fees are non -refundable (except security deposit ) and the 
University reserves the right to review the fee structure from time 
to time. Any revision of fees would be uniformly applicable to all 
students at the University. 
Financial Assistance (Loan) 
FAST, being a non -profit organization, charges subsidized fees 
from all its students. Realizing that even the subsidized fee may  
not be affordable for some of its students. FAST tries to arrange 
financial assistance in the form of loan for such indigent students. 
This assistance is subject to renewal every semester in the light 
of the student's academic performance and financial need. The 
financial ass istance is limited to tuition fees only and is 
discontinued if the student's CGPA falls below 2.00 for 
undergraduate degree and 2.5 for graduate degree. 
The repayment of loan starts three months after graduation or 
getting a job, whichever is earlier. The total amount must  be 
repaid within a period of four years after graduation. Students are 
required to sign to this effect. 
All those who are admitted and are in real need of financial 
assistance should apply on the prescribed Financial Aid form. A 
notice to this effect will be posted on the notice board.
